stem: A junior doctor is preparing to perform a lumbar puncture in a child positioned on their side with the hips and knees flexed, and palpates both posterior-superior iliac crests before drawing an imaginary line between them. What does this landmark indicate?

options.text: It intersects L4, helping select the L3/L4 or L4/L5 space for needle insertion
It intersects L2, so the needle should be inserted at L1/L2
It guides the choice between iodine and chlorhexidine skin prep
It indicates the needle should be directed away from the umbilicus
It is assessed only after cerebrospinal fluid has been collected

explanation: The posterior-superior iliac crest line intersects L4, which helps identify the L3/L4 or L4/L5 interspace for lumbar puncture.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: A line between the posterior-superior iliac crests is used as a surface landmark to locate L4 and guide safe lumbar puncture level selection.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the intercristal line is used to identify L4 and then choose the L3/L4 or L4/L5 interspace for needle insertion.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the intercristal line is not taken to intersect L2, and L1/L2 is not the intended lumbar puncture level here.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because skin antiseptic choice is separate from anatomical landmark identification for lumbar puncture.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because needle direction is a separate procedural step; the landmark identifies the vertebral level, not the direction of insertion.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because this landmark is used before insertion to select the puncture site, not after cerebrospinal fluid collection.
